properties.name: Any design can say how its premises support a conclusion (all of them, any one, k of n, or a named inference rule), and reflow2 checks that the conclusion's status follows
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-10-14: "I want to expand reflow2/flo2 to be able to do lines of reasoning, the graph is the proof, and inference steps for every design." He asked it first as a question: "would having both Operation: Modus Ponens and a check in reflow2 checks that Q actually follows from P and P → Q improve any design that reflow2 does?"

WHAT MUST BE TRUE:
1. AN INFERENCE STEP CAN BE STATED: the rule by which premises support a conclusion. The rule is one of all (AND), any one (OR), k of n, or a named rule such as modus ponens. It is a record of its own, an Inference, between the premises and the conclusion (dec:an-inference-is-a-record-between-premises-and-conclusion, his choice 2026-10-14), so its warrant can itself be challenged, verified or go stale.
2. ALL (AND) STAYS THE DEFAULT AND SAYS NOTHING. Every existing design reads exactly as it does today. Delivery already rolls up by an unwritten AND (req:decomposition-covers-its-parent); this writes it down and puts OR and k-of-n beside it.
3. THE CHECK IS OVER STATUSES. Given each premise's status and the step's rule, does the conclusion's claimed status follow? It is a mechanical truth-table check over recorded statuses and needs no formal language. It checks the FORM only:
   - whether each premise is true stays with verification;
   - whether the children cover the parent stays a question put to the person, never a model's judgement.
4. THE ROLL-UP AND THE CHANGE WALK HONOUR THE RULE, so losing a premise is reported as BROKEN (no support remains) or WEAKENED (it still stands on another path).
5. THE RULE IS A DECLARED RULE THE CODE RUNS (req:reflow2s-code-reasons-from-the-declared-meanings-and-every-derived-relationship-is-a-declared-rule), not logic hidden in a report.
6. IT IS ADDITIVE TO WHAT CLIENTS SEE: nothing is removed or renamed. The retirement rule is not involved.

IT ANSWERS AN OPEN QUESTION IN ACCEPTED INTENT: req:assumptions-are-first-class asks what edge carries "rests on". The precedent is budgets: req:a-budget-says-whether-its-parts-add-up-or-run-along-a-path did this for quantities, and this does it for logic. Engineering precedent: fault-tree AND/OR gates, and the Strategy node of an assurance case in Goal Structuring Notation.

LIMIT, stated so nobody over-reads it: a false premise passes the check. What the step gains is that its warrant becomes something a person can challenge.

SHOWN WHEN: on a real design, a claim with redundant support is marked "any one", one support is removed, and reflow2 reports the claim weakened and still standing. Then the last support is removed and it reports the claim broken. An unmarked design reports exactly as before.

WHAT COULD BE TAKEN AWAY INSTEAD (rule:before-a-structural-addition-ask-what-could-be-taken-away), asked 2026-10-14. Anthony, agreeing with the answer: "I agree, record the answer on requirement C".

NOTHING COULD BE. Nothing built, required or ruled is made unnecessary by this.
- What it changes in the living system: the roll-up's hard-coded "a parent is delivered when every child is" (report.rs, quoted in req:decomposition-covers-its-parent) becomes a declared rule, ALL, that behaves the same by default. It is replaced, not removed.
- Considered and kept:
  - the separate argument record types (claim, warrant, objection), option (d) of dec:idea-reflow2-designs-a-line-of-reasoning-an-argument-an-experiment-a-paper-a-legal-case. They were never built, so there is nothing to remove. They were set aside when req:a-design-holds-a-line-of-reasoning was accepted "with reflow2's own vocabulary".
  - a separate Assumption record type, still open in req:assumptions-are-first-class. This requirement answers only that requirement's edge question (what carries "rests on"), not its node-type question. An assumption that fails is a change in the world, while a violated constraint is a defect in the design. Folding one into the other would blur the distinction that requirement exists to keep, so that question stays open for its own decision.
